{{Short description|Soviet mathematician}}
'''Isidor Pavlovich Natanson''' ({{langx|ru|Исидор Павлович Натансон}}; February 8, 1906 in [[Zurich]] &ndash; July 3, 1964 in [[Leningrad]]) was a [[Switzerland|Swiss]]-born [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] [[mathematician]] known for contributions to [[real analysis]] and [[constructive function theory]], in particular, for his textbooks on these subjects.<ref>{{cite journal|volume=20|issue=1|first1=B.Z.|last1= Vulikh|first2=M.K.|last2= Gavurin|first3=S. M.|last3= Lozinskii|year= 1965|journal= Russ. Math. Surv.|page=169|doi=10.1070/RM1965v020n01ABEH004142|title=Isidor Pavlovich Natanson (obituary)|bibcode=1965RuMaS..20..169V|mr=0172783|s2cid=250831189}}</ref> His son, Garal'd Natanson (1930&ndash;2003), was also a known mathematician.<ref>{{cite journal|mr=2106648|author=Babich, V. M.|author2=Vershik, A. M.|author3=Videnskiĭ, V. S.|display-authors=etal |title=Garalʹd Isidorovich Natanson (obituary)|journal=Russian Math. Surveys|volume=59|year=2004|issue=4|pages=771&ndash;776|doi=10.1070/RM2004v059n04ABEH000761|bibcode=2004RuMaS..59..771B|s2cid=250919574 }}</ref>
